Rechecked against pp-07 and LP-12 as asked; the attestation stands, on the description's own clause 'reading content where the question asks about shape'. TM-07's stem asks why the writer NUMBERS the helpers 'a second, a third, a fourth, a fifth', which is the form of lines 27-29, and its key ('make the crowd grow bigger with every word') is that form's effect. The option reads the list's content (each helper has a job) as orderliness. pp-07's key is about what the numbers report (talk changing as it passes on), and LP-12's technique is withheld interiority, a point-of-view choice. Neither asks about form, so the same entry was refused there. Caveat for the library: the entry's description is worded around its one example (short sentence, landing suddenly). If it is meant to be read literally, this seat fails as well, and the description should be widened to name lists and counts before more carriers are put under it.

en-parallel-read-as-sequence names a specific shape: 'two parallel descriptions of one thing', the same subject given twice from two vantages, read as two moments. Lines 27-29 are not two descriptions of one subject; they are five different helpers with five different jobs (hold the chair, help him up, hand a nail, pass the hammer). Reading a simultaneous count as stages in time is the right mechanism, but this entry's description does not cover it. It needs either a widened description or a different entry.
